messages:
Sanjay: alerting — we're seeing a fast ramp of OOMs from the paged-KV allocator on us-west-2 inference nodes, started ~10m ago. ~12 pods crashed, node flaps on gpu-pool-3. Nvidia/driver errors in logs: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED and CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY. dmesg includes oom_kill events referencing inference_worker.

Ellie: ack. any customer impact yet? do we have a way to triage which models/tenants are affected?

Mike: looking now — Prom query: sum(rate(runtime_pod_oom_total[5m])) by (node) shows spike on gpu-node-{13..16}. Also seeing increased page-faults: runtime_paged_attn_faults_total up ~8x. Top model by error: rdx-open-7b (long-context). Customer-facing errors: 4 requests returned 503 with 'executor error: OOM' in logs (customer ids: C-234, C-998).

oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: INC-224500 - paged-KV mem-bleed → oncall. Assigned: Sanjay. Severity: P1. Runbook: eng-runtime / paged-kv-ooms.

Sanjay: immediate plan: 1) collect full CUDA dump and coredumps from one crashed pod 2) temporarily increase kv eviction aggressiveness + drop paging 3) roll small canary to quantized model variant for affected model 4) schedule node cordon/drain if node continues to flap. executing step 1 now.

Kai: I'll take step 2/3. For eviction we can bump runtime config: 
``` 
PATCH /api/v1/runtime/config
{
  "kv_eviction_threshold": 0.65,
  "kv_hot_warm_ratio": 0.2,
  "paging_enabled": false
}
```
This will force more frequent prefix eviction and disable paging for new pods; needs a rollout.

Ellie: be careful disabling paging globally — can increase latency. Prefer targetting the model route if we can. Is per-model runtime config supported for that model?

Mike: yes we have per-route overrides. CLI to update route: 
```
redwood routes update --route rdx-open-7b --set runtime.paging.enabled=false --set runtime.kv.eviction_threshold=0.65
```
I'll apply to the failing route first, then monitor.

Sanjay: collecting dump — attaching partial logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T22:05:12Z] runtime: Alloc failed: requested 2147483648 bytes
[2026-03-15T22:05:12Z] cuda: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED (0x3e) in gemm
[2026-03-15T22:05:12Z] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 3456 (inference_worker)
```

Mike: applied per-route override for rdx-open-7b and kicked canary roll to quantized-8bit variant (rdx-open-7b-quant). Rolling 3 pods to start. Metrics to watch: runtime_token_latency_p50, runtime_pod_oom_total, runtime_error_rate.

Sanjay: doing pod-level collection: 
```
kubectl -n inference exec -it inference-pod-3456 -- bash -c "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv"
kubectl -n inference logs inference-pod-3456 --previous > /tmp/pod-3456-prev.log
gcore -o /tmp/core.inference 3456 || true
```

Ellie: customer comms — we should surface a short note to the support status page: "We are experiencing memory-related failures affecting a subset of inference workloads in US-WEST-2. Mitigation is in progress; some requests may see 503s or increased latency." Anyone from support to draft?

pagerduty: Support notified. Draft prepared, waiting for ops ack.

Kai: after override, we've seen 3 of 3 canary pods come up healthy. Pod OOMs dropped to zero on those pods. However node-level fragmentation persists on gpu-node-14 — still observing periodic flaps (~1 every 8m). Suspect allocator fragmentation slow-creep (tiny slab mis-sizes + paged attention hot paths).

Mike: getting a heapmap from runtime: KV slab fragmentation at ~78% on node-14, but at 42% on node-15. There's a growing number of small, non-evictable slots (~30k). Might be a pattern introduced by recent attention-paging change.

Sanjay: temp mitigation for node flaps: cordon gpu-node-14 and migrate pods off it. Then force restart the allocator service on that node to free internal bitmaps. Steps: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-14
kubectl drain gpu-node-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
ssh ops@gpu-node-14 'systemctl restart redwood-runtime' || true
```
I'll run the cordon now.

Ellie: please include a note in the incident timeline when you cordon — we need to track customer impact windows.

Sanjay: cordoned and started drain. Migration in progress — kube events show pods rescheduled. Node still showing OOM on restart attempts, proceeding to systemctl restart now.

incident-bot: Updated incident INC-224500 — mitigation: per-route paging disabled for rdx-open-7b, canary rolled to rdx-open-7b-quant, node gpu-node-14 cordoned & draining. Severity remains P1.

Kai: after restart, allocator service came up clean; fragmentation dropped to 31% on node-14. No additional flaps in the last 6 minutes. We'll keep node cordoned until stabilization window of 30m.

Mike: customer impact count: 9 requests failed across 3 customers in last 20m, 0 data exfiltration, retries succeeded for most after fallback to quantized canary. Recording in ticket: C-234, C-998, C-412.

Ellie: please run a short postmortem checklist: 1) collect all coredumps + cuda logs (Sanjay) 2) capture runtime config diff and operator changes (Kai) 3) snapshot metrics and graph images (Mike) 4) draft customer-facing blurb (Support).

Sanjay: uploading artifacts to /incidents/224500/artifacts/ — cores, pod logs, nvidia-smi, runtime heapmaps. Paste link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/224500/artifacts (internal).

Kai: plan for next steps: 1) revert the attention-paging change from last week's internal rollout and monitor for 48h, 2) add guardrail to allocator to proactively defragment small-slot accumulation (follow-up ticket to eng-runtime), 3) surface an Optimize suggestion to affected customers to pin to quantized variant if latency acceptable. Creating tickets.

Mike: creating follow-up task RT-224500-1: "investigate paged-attn allocator fragmentation" and RT-224500-2: "allocator guardrail: small-slot compaction". Linking to incident.

Ellie: handing off to Kai for night coverage in 5m. Sanjay — can you summarise current mitigations for the handoff note?

Sanjay: handoff summary: 
- Current state: node gpu-node-14 cordoned, drain complete, allocator restart done. Per-route paging disabled for rdx-open-7b; canary quantized variant rolled and healthy. OOMs on canary = 0 in last 15m.
- Artifacts: cores + logs uploaded.
- Action items for oncall: keep node cordoned for 30m stabilization, monitor runtime_pod_oom_total and paged_attn_faults. If flaps resume, escalate to infra to repro on baremetal and consider rolling kernel/driver update.
- Customer impact: 3 customers affected briefly, support notified.

Kai: taking over. I'll keep the node cordoned and watch for 2h, will escalate if fragmentation climbs >60% again. Adding status to the incident and pinging infra oncall for a possible allocator patch tomorrow. Thanks all.

incident-bot: Incident INC-224500 updated: oncall handoff from Sanjay to Kai. Primary mitigations in place.

Ellie: thanks — we'll convert this to a postmortem if root cause confirms allocator regression. Good job getting the canary out quickly. :thumbsup:

Sanjay: handing off. Leaving open for monitoring.

Kai: noted — will post final stabilization note in ~2h or sooner if anything changes.

pagerduty: Support posted status update to customers: "Mitigation in place; some requests may briefly have experienced 503s. We are monitoring."
